description.value:
You can harvest body parts from slain creatures and graft them onto your companion to give it new capabilities. You use your Medicine in place of the usual skill for harvesting each creature type. However, the attempt only succeeds if you meet the DC for a pristine ingredient.

You can graft or remove body parts to your companion as part of completing a Short or Long Rest. The maximum number of grafted body parts is two and you cannot choose the same creature type more than once. You automatically preserve any body parts that aren't currently grafted, though you need a method of storing and carrying them to bring them with you.

Your companion gains the ability associated with each grafted body part as per the list below.

  • Aberration. Your companion's Intelligence is replaced with that of the aberration, up to a maximum of 20. Additionally, it gains a new ability, which it can use in place of its slam attack: Psychic Rend: 60 ft range, Intelligence Saving Throw: DC equals your spell save DC. Failure: 1d6 + the aberration's proficiency + your companion's Intelligence modifier psychic damage.
  • Beast. Your companion's Strength or Dexterity (your choice) is replaced with that of the beast, up to a maximum of 20, and your companion can use its Dexterity in place of its Strength for melee damage rolls with its slam. Additionally, your companion gains any special movement type of the harvested creature, equal to its own Speed.
  • Construct. Your companion's AC is replaced with that of the harvested creature, up to a maximum of 20.
  • Dragon. Your companion gains a breath weapon which it can use as an Action. The damage type and shape of the breath weapon is the same as that of the dragon. The size of the breath weapon is 30 feet if it is a cone and 5 x 60 feet if it is a line. The damage is equal to that of your companion's death burst feature + the Proficiency of the dragon.
  • Once has used its breath weapon, you have to roll a d6 at the start of each of your turns. On a roll of 5 or 6, it regains its use of this feature.
  • Elemental. Your companion gains a damage Resistance based on the elemental's Immunity. If the elemental has multiple Immunities, you choose which one to use. Additionally, your companion deals bonus damage of the same type equal to the elemental's Proficiency when it hits with its slam attack.
  • Fey. Your companion's alignment and its Charisma is replaced with that of the fey, up to a maximum of 20. Your companion also gains its own personality, based on that of the fey, and may act on its own when not currently ordered to do something.
  • Additionally, if your companion has to make a Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, it adds half the fey's Proficiency (rounded down). This augmentation is exclusive with those gained from fiends.
  • Fiend. Your companion's alignment and two Ability Scores of your choice are replaced with those of the fiend. Your companion also gains its own personality, based on that of the fiend, and may act on its own when not currently ordered to do something.
  • Additionally, your companion regenerates hit points equal to the fiend's Proficiency at the start of each of its turn, unless it has taken radiant damage since its last turn. This augmentation is exclusive with those gained from fey.
  • Giant. Your companion's Strength is replaced with that of the giant, up to a maximum of 20. Additionally, your companion's size changes to Large and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws. When your companion hits with its slam attack, it deals additional damage of the same type equal to the giant's Proficiency.
  • Ooze. Your companion's Constitution is replaced with that of the ooze, up to a maximum of 20. Additionally, its current and maximum hit points increase by four times the ooze's Proficiency and it can spend 5 feet of its movement to remove the Grappled or Restrained condition from itself.
  • Plant. Your companion's current and maximum hit points increase by double the plant's Proficiency. Additionally, the reach of its slam attack increases by 10 feet. Once per turn, a creature hit by your companion's slam attack has to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is Grappled by your companion. Any creature that starts its turn Grappled in this manner, takes bludgeoning damage equal to the plant's Proficiency.
  • Undead. As part of the Bonus Action used to command it, you can tell your companion to exude an aura of necrotic energy. When you do so, you can exempt a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier from the effect. On subsequent turns, you can deactivate the aura the same way.
  • The size of the aura is 10 feet, but increases to 20 feet if the undead's CR was 10 or higher, and to 30 feet if its CR was 20 or higher.
  • Any creature that ends its turn in the aura or enters it for the first time on a turn, takes necrotic damage equal to the undead's proficiency.
